name: Tajikistan

chips.label: Earned prosperity
chips.why: Institutions roughly match or exceed what income predicts - durable.
chips.rule: MI residual vs. the log-GDP regression (the durability gap): below -0.03 → granted, otherwise earned (a ±0.03 tolerance treats near-zero gaps as in-line).

chips.label: Lopsided · weakest: Economic Complexity
chips.why: Spread between the strongest and weakest pillar - the country's structural shape.

verdict: Mixed structural profile - prosperity roughly in line with institutions - lopsided (economic complexity the weak point).

checks.title: Durability gate
checks.headline: earned-vs-granted +0.02
checks.detail: Prosperity sits roughly in line with institutions. No durability warning here.

checks.title: Weakest link
checks.headline: Economic Complexity is lowest
checks.detail: Economic Complexity is the pillar dragging the score down. A chain breaks at its weakest link, so this is where the structural risk concentrates.

checks.title: Room to rise
checks.headline: low base
checks.detail: Starting from a low institutional base, the country is structurally eligible to climb. This is eligibility, not a forecast - the effect only showed up strongly in the 2000s global growth wave.

safeguards.name: Durability Gate (P4-P1 gap)
safeguards.headline: income-institutions gap +0.27 · borderline
safeguards.detail: Economic Structure-Institutions gap = 0.273 in the indeterminate band (0.2, 0.28): the N=21 data is UNIDENTIFIED here (empty zone between the absorber and crisis clusters). Above every confirmed absorber but below the crisis floor - elevated WATCH, not a verdict; a further institutional backslide would tip it into the flag.
safeguards.modification: Treat as elevated watch; insufficient validated evidence to call. Monitor P1 vs P4.
safeguards.why: Independently derived on 21 crisis/absorber cases: the level gap between income (P4) and institutions (P1) separated real crises from shock-absorbers at 83% sensitivity / 100% specificity. When income has outrun institutions, the state is structurally crisis-prone under shock - 'granted/fragile'.

safeguards.name: Rentier Capture (Bidirectional)
safeguards.headline: below 15% of GDP · no penalty
safeguards.detail: Resource rents 9.1% of GDP -> below 15% (no penalty).
safeguards.why: Resource rents can inflate or hollow out measured institutional quality (Timor-Leste), or buy elite cohesion in a low-capacity state (Nigeria/Gulf). Graded E-1 (material, >15% of GDP) / E-2 (severe, >25%); severe rents make P1 unreliable.

safeguards.name: External Administration
safeguards.headline: needs curated input
safeguards.why: Bosnia's WGI institutional scores under the Dayton OHR sat above Croatia's and Serbia's - the administrator's competence, not indigenous capacity, was being measured. The safeguard discounts raw P1 where an external administrator governs.

safeguards.name: Capacity Gate
safeguards.headline: needs curated input
safeguards.detail: Institutions = 0.345, successors = N/A. Gate not triggered.
safeguards.why: Sudan split into just two successor states - a low fragment count that would normally read as manageable - yet produced the worst outcome in the sample, because institutional capacity (P1) was far below the bottom third. Low count is not safety when P1 is that low.

safeguards.name: Reversal Risk
safeguards.headline: needs curated input
safeguards.why: The framework predicted Tunisia's initial positive trajectory but missed the 2021 presidential self-coup. Democratic transitions with weak economic delivery are flagged as reversal-prone rather than assumed durable.

safeguards.name: Predatory Neighbor / Exogenous Shock
safeguards.headline: needs curated input
safeguards.detail: No significant predatory neighbor threat identified.
safeguards.why: A structurally sound state can be overrun from outside. The safeguard separates a country's endogenous trajectory from vulnerability to an aggressive neighbour or external shock, so the outcome isn't misread as internally generated.

safeguards.name: Sub-State Turbulence
safeguards.headline: needs curated input
safeguards.why: A state can survive intact while carrying chronic, managed instability - repeated executive collapses, high anti-system voting, sharp regional divergence. This is a management-load signal, not a collapse indicator.

safeguards.name: Suppression vs Prevention
safeguards.headline: needs curated input
safeguards.why: Suppression and prevention looked identical until this safeguard split them into tiers: military suppression (Tier 1) doesn't resolve the underlying mismatch; institutional/legal suppression (Tier 2) de-escalates; porosity/power-sharing (Tier 3) addresses it by design. Re-suppression after a porosity period is the worst path.

safeguards.name: Porosity-with-Backstop
safeguards.headline: needs curated input
safeguards.why: The framework's most genuinely novel prediction: when a great-power patron backstops a state's territorial integrity, an internal secession tends to end in re-suppression and partial reconsolidation, not permanent independence.

strategy.explanation: P1 = 0.345. System manages complexity through control rather than diffusion. Suppression tier: Military/authoritarian suppression.
strategy.failure_mode: Violent fragmentation when control mechanisms weaken

flags: WARNING: P1 below median - elevated structural risk
CRITICAL: Pillar spread 0.534 - extreme configuration imbalance

structural_vulnerability.reading: INDETERMINATE - gap sits in the empty band between the validated absorber ceiling and crisis floor; above every confirmed absorber but below the crisis floor. Elevated watch, not a verdict.

vulnerability.summary: Risk level: HIGH. P1 = 0.345, spread = 0.534, 1 safeguards active.

accountability_gap.caveat: HYPOTHESIS (V3.2) - informational; orthogonal to the durability gap; no crisis validation yet.
